items.headline: Delhi Police: reel makers not covered as journalists
items.text: Answering four press groups' Supreme Court petitions over protest coverage, Delhi Police said its protections for journalists don't cover reel makers or influencers. Police deny stopping reporters or seizing equipment.

photo.alt: A tall red and beige stone instrument with arched openings, on a lawn.
photo.caption: The Jantar Mantar observatory in New Delhi; journalists' complaints include coverage of protests near it on 3 October. Photo from 2017.

items.headline: Keralam: 15,627 posts taken down in six months
items.text: Keralam's home minister told the Assembly 15,627 posts or links were taken down on police requests in the new government's first six months, with 3,472 cases filed. He said they were fabricated or manipulated.

photo.alt: A long white colonnaded building with a red-tiled tower behind palm trees and a gate.
photo.caption: The Kerala Legislative Assembly building (Niyamasabha) in Thiruvananthapuram, in 2010. File photo.

items.headline: High Court grants Azam Khan interim bail
items.text: The Allahabad High Court bailed former UP minister Azam Khan until 10 Dec, saying the ED arrested him at a jail gate without written grounds. The ED says it followed procedure.

photo.alt: A large cream stone court building with a pediment, red-tiled roofs and an Indian flag, behind lawns and potted plants.
photo.caption: The Allahabad High Court in Prayagraj, in 2009. File photo.

items.headline: UN: at least 2,230 civilians killed this year
items.text: The UN rights office verified at least 2,230 civilian deaths in Sudan from January to October, over 1,630 by drone strikes, mostly in Kordofan. No army or RSF response was reported.

photo.alt: Makeshift shelters of sticks, cloth and plastic on dry red ground under a blue sky.
photo.caption: Makeshift shelters at Intifada transit camp near Nyala, South Darfur, in 2005. File photo.

items.headline: UN: 2026 deadliest year for Ukraine's civilians
items.text: UN monitors say 372 civilians were killed in Ukraine in October, and more died in 2026's first ten months than in all of 2025. Russia says Ukrainian strikes killed civilians in occupied areas.

photo.alt: A single-storey public building with a red roof and flags, behind a fence and a road.
photo.caption: The public services centre in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, in 2025; the UN report cites the 2 Nov bombing of a school in the village. File photo.

items.headline: UN: 514 killed in Haiti's anti-gang operations
items.text: The UN rights office says 514 people were killed in security operations against gangs in July–September, and 4,595 by armed violence this year. No Haitian government response was reported.

photo.alt: A busy street with crowds walking past stalls of clothes and goods, shop signs and low buildings.
photo.caption: A street in Port-au-Prince in 2012. File photo.

items.headline: Over 245 held at Manila summit protests
items.text: Police detained at least 245 people protesting during the ASEAN summit and Trump's visit, held three days without charge, HRW says. Police said the street protests were unauthorised.

photo.alt: A wet city street beside a white monument plaza and trees, with a large 'Welcome to ASEAN Community' banner.
photo.caption: Liwasang Bonifacio plaza in Manila, with an ASEAN banner, in 2017. File photo of the protest site.

items.headline: Gaza ceasefire near collapse, Board of Peace warns
items.text: The US-backed Board of Peace told the UN Security Council the truce may collapse, saying Israel blocks winter supplies and Gaza's interim administration and both sides miss commitments. No Israeli or Hamas response was reported.

photo.alt: People in dark clothing stand among plastic-sheet tents in heavy rain on muddy ground.
photo.caption: Flooded tents of displaced Palestinians after heavy rain in Deir el-Balah, Gaza, in 2025. File photo.
photo.credit: Ashraf Amra / UNRWA, via Wikimedia Commons

items.headline: Public workers march across France over pay
items.text: Public-sector workers, pupils and students marched across France on 17 Nov; the interior ministry counted 146,000, the CGT union just over 500,000. The government says debt leaves little room for raises.

photo.alt: A bronze statue of a woman holding an olive branch on a tall stone monument, against a blue sky.
photo.caption: The Monument to the Republic at Place de la République, Paris, a usual rally point, in 2026. File photo.
